docs.title: rn-forge-fastapi
docs.text:
rn-forge-fastapi wires rn-forge-web into FastAPI. The web package settles what goes on the wire; this package is the FastAPI-shaped plumbing that puts it there, so every FastAPI application built on the kit spells the same six adapters the same way.

It provides:

  • problem — register_problem_handlers: every error, including FastAPI's own 404, 405 and 422, rendered as an RFC 9457 application/problem+json body
  • openapi — the problem-response repair FastApiApp.openapi() applies, so the document declares the error responses the app sends, and operation_id, the shared operationId convention
  • dependencies — page_params, require_idempotency_key and require_if_match
  • health — health_router, serving /healthz and /readyz
  • auth — bearer_auth, basic_auth and requires, producing rn-forge-auth's Principal

docs.title: Where it sits
docs.text:
commons ──► web ──► auth ──► django
                          └───► fastapi

It depends on rn-forge-web, rn-forge-auth and FastAPI, and never imports rn_forge.django, rn_forge.cli or rn_forge.tooling. uv run lint-imports proves it.

Adapt, do not re-decide. A status code, a header name or an encoding decided here would be a divergence from the Django stack by definition, so there are none. This package's test suite runs the rn-forge-web conformance table through a FastAPI application built from these adapters, with no skips.

docs.title: Added
docs.text:
• The /auth surface over rn-forge-auth. auth_router(config, prefix="/auth"), configured by AuthRoutesConfig, returns an APIRouter serving providers, login/{provider}, callback/{provider}, session, logout, logout/all, backchannel-logout/{provider} and login/password over LoginFlow, with the responses, error codes and __Host-login-tx cookie of the Django binding. The development provider exists only with debug=True. AuthRoutesConfig raises ValueError without a problem_type_base. The stores' synchronous calls and the Authlib providers run in the thread pool. The auth guide describes the setup, configuration defaults and the protocols an application implements.
  • Login sessions. SessionMiddleware(sessions=sessions_for(config)) resolves the session once per request over a SessionStore behind the __Host-session cookie, extends the 30-minute idle expiry and refreshes the cookie on every request except GET /auth/session, and clears a cookie that names no valid session. Sessions.read enforces the 12-hour absolute timeout and deletes a session whose version differs from its account's, whose account is inactive or whose session_ref is revoked. active_session(request) returns the resolved session, and await rotate_session(request) gives it a new ID after a privilege change. The middleware takes untouched_paths, login_path and csrf_exempt_prefixes for a router mounted under another prefix.
  • Synchronizer-token CSRF protection. SessionMiddleware checks an unsafe request that carries the __Host-session cookie (live, anonymous or stale), or goes to /auth/login/password, and never back-channel logout; a cookie-less request to an application route is left alone. The X-XSRF-TOKEN header must equal, in constant time, the token stored for the session, which the readable XSRF-TOKEN cookie carries. The Origin (or Referer over HTTPS) must be the request's own origin or one of trusted_origins, Sec-Fetch-Site: cross-site is rejected, forwarded scheme and host count only from a trusted_proxies peer, and a Bearer Authorization header skips the check. A failure is the 403 csrf-failed problem. Tokens live in a CsrfStore keyed by session ID: InMemoryCsrfStore, and RedisCsrfStore. GET /auth/session always sets the cookie, starting a 10-minute anonymous session when there is no session, so login is protected. Login replaces the session ID and the token, logout starts a new anonymous session, and rotate_session carries the token to the new ID.
  • Rate limits on /auth/login/password (per client and per submitted username) and the callback routes (per client), with the defaults of the Django binding, set by AuthRoutesConfig's limiter, password_client_limit, password_account_limit and callback_client_limit (RateLimit(limit, window), or None for no limit). A limited request is the too-many-requests problem, 429 with Retry-After. InMemoryRateLimiter counts in a fixed window; RedisRateLimiter counts with INCR and EXPIRE. The client is the connection's peer, or the nearest address in X-Forwarded-For that is not a trusted proxy when the peer is in trusted_proxies.
  • Authentication and authorization dependencies. current_principal(bearer=None) yields the session Principal (roles and permissions from the account's authorization context, auth_time and amr from the session) or the bearer one; a request with an Authorization header is authenticated by bearer alone, so an invalid token is a 401 even with a valid session cookie. requires_permission(authenticate, key, action, action_map=None) enforces requirement_for(key, action). PolicyGuard(policy, hides_existence=False) applies a ResourcePolicy: scope(principal, action, query) narrows a query of any type, and check(principal, action, obj) returns the object or raises 403, or 404 when hides_existence is true.
  • Audit events on the rn_forge.audit.auth channel, with the names and fields of the Django binding: login.success, login.failure, logout, logout.all, logout.backchannel, account.rejected, account.disabled and rate_limited from the routes, and authorization.denied from requires, requires_permission and PolicyGuard. A provisioning AccountResolver records account.provisioned with rn_forge.auth.audit.
  • The redis extra, which names rn-forge-auth[redis]. Outside debug, auth_router and Sessions refuse in-memory session, transaction, replay, CSRF and rate-limit stores with a RuntimeError; the Redis stores are rn_forge.auth.redis and, for CSRF tokens and the rate limiter, the rn_forge.fastapi.auth.redis module, which the package facade does not import.
  • Tests tag each security control of rn_forge.auth.conformance with @pytest.mark.security_control, and fail when a control has no test.

docs.title: Changed
docs.text:
• rn_forge.fastapi.auth is a package; bearer_auth, basic_auth and requires import from it as before.
  • Breaking: bearer_auth() takes accounts (an AccountResolver) and contexts (an AuthorizationContextProvider), and optionally scope_map. It resolves the token's (issuer, subject) with accounts.lookup, never provisions, and answers 401 for an unlinked or inactive account. The principal's subject is the account ID; roles, tenant and attributes come from the context, and permissions are the context's limited by the token's scopes. It returns a BearerAuth dependency.
  • Breaking: depends on rn-forge-auth and imports Principal, Requirement and the authenticator contracts from it. The oidc extra names rn-forge-auth[oidc] instead of rn-forge-web[auth].
  • The package declares the MIT licence and is published to PyPI.

docs.title: Changed
docs.text: • Requires its rn-forge dependencies by version range from pykit's index (ADR-0004), not by git URL.

docs.title: Fixed
docs.text: • FastApiApp turns off FastAPI's native tracing (0.142 and later) unless the application passes telemetry=, so AppConfig(tracing=False) records no server spans.

docs.title: Changed

docs.title: Added
docs.text:
• Soft delete in AIP-164's shape: soft_delete_router (DELETE {collection}/{id} answering 200 with the resource, and POST {collection}/{id}:undelete), the SoftDeleteStore protocol and SoftDeleteState, and show_deleted_param(), all exported from rn_forge.fastapi.
  • read_mask_param(model) and masked(page, mask) for the readMask query parameter. batch_get_router takes a new read_mask parameter (default True) and applies the mask.
  • batch_get_router (GET :batchGet) and batch_update_router (POST :batchUpdate, one JSON Merge Patch and optional ifMatch per item) in rn_forge.fastapi.transfer, with the BatchGetStore, BatchUpdateStore and Current protocols. batch_update_router takes require_if_match and codec.
  • Route factories in rn_forge.fastapi.transfer that match rn-forge-django's transfer mixins: import_router (POST :import), import_template_router (GET :importTemplate), batch_create_router (POST :batchCreate) and batch_delete_router (POST :batchDelete). Each takes a dependency returning a store (ImportStore, TemplateSource, BatchCreateStore, BatchDeleteStore), max_rows and dependencies=. tabular_export applies the export cap inside an application's own list route. RowsResult gains total, read_rows takes formats= and raises ValueError with the shared unsupported and unreadable file details. A store raises RowsInvalid (422) or ItemsDenied (403) from rn-forge-web for a failure only it can find. The factories answer the shared 422s: a missing file, a missing or empty list, and a row cap. The transfer guide shows a complete resource over rn-forge-sqlalchemy's upsert and keyset.
  • JSON Merge Patch (RFC 7396) binding: merge_patch_body() checks the application/merge-patch+json media type (415 with Accept-Patch) and returns the raw body, merge_into(model, current, body) parses it, merges and validates against a pydantic model, and merge_patch_openapi() declares the request body. Declare merge_patch_body() before require_if_match and call check_precondition before merge_into. A null on a non-nullable field renders This field may not be null.

docs.title: Changed
docs.text:
• Breaking: order_by_param describes orderBy as a comma-separated list of fields and names the sortable fields. It described one field. It returns every term, as parse_order_by in rn-forge-web now accepts several and rejects a repeated field with 400.
  • read_rows picks the format from the file extension, and uses the content type only when the file name has none, as rn-forge-django does. A .pdf sent as text/csv is now unsupported.

docs.text:
• Installation — how a consumer declares the dependency, and why uv add is not it.
  • Quickstart — the four lines every application starts with.
  • Wiring an application — the whole wiring module, the rules it depends on, and what an application still writes itself.
  • Tabular export and import — the transfer extra: CSV and xlsx download, validated upload.

The normative wire contract is rn-forge-web's API conventions page. This package implements it; it does not restate it.

docs.title: Auth
docs.text:
rn_forge.fastapi.auth binds the login, session, CSRF and authorization design of rn-forge-auth (a separate package, which holds the framework-neutral contracts, login flows, session and replay stores and the OIDC adapter) to FastAPI. It serves a browser single-page application through a server-side session, and API clients through bearer tokens, with one account and one authorization model behind both. rn-forge-auth documents the providers and stores; this page documents the FastAPI side. The Django binding in rn-forge-django serves the same routes, responses and audit events.

The session, CSRF and rate-limit state is shared by every worker, so outside development it lives in Redis. Install rn-forge-fastapi with the redis extra, and with oidc for OIDC login or JWKS bearer tokens.

docs.title: Setup
docs.text:
An end-to-end configuration with one OIDC provider, local password login and, in development, a fixture-account provider:

# myapp/auth_config.py
from redis import Redis
from rn_forge.auth import (
    AuthorizationContextCache,
    DevelopmentAccount,
    DevelopmentIdentityProvider,
    PasswordIdentityProvider,
)
from rn_forge.auth.oidc import OidcProvider
from rn_forge.auth.redis import (
    RedisAuthorizationVersions,
    RedisReplayStore,
    RedisSessionStore,
    RedisTransactionStore,
)
from rn_forge.fastapi.auth import AuthRoutesConfig
from rn_forge.fastapi.auth.redis import RedisCsrfStore, RedisRateLimiter

from myapp.accounts import MyAccountResolver, MyAccountState, MyContexts, check_password

DEBUG = False
redis = Redis.from_url("redis://localhost:6379/0")

contexts = AuthorizationContextCache(
    MyContexts(),
    versions=RedisAuthorizationVersions(redis),
    writer=MyAccountState(),
)

providers = {
    "acme": OidcProvider(
        id="acme",
        issuer="https://login.example.com/tenant/v2.0",
        client_id="orders-web",
        client_secret="...",
        redirect_uri="https://app.example.com/auth/callback/acme",
    ),
    "password": PasswordIdentityProvider(check_password),
}
if DEBUG:
    providers["development"] = DevelopmentIdentityProvider(
        [DevelopmentAccount("alice", name="Alice")], debug=True
    )

config = AuthRoutesConfig(
    providers=providers,
    accounts=MyAccountResolver(),
    contexts=contexts,
    account_state=contexts,  # writes through to MyAccountState
    problem_type_base="https://errors.example.com/",
    return_to_prefixes=["/app"],
    default_return_to="/app",
    provider_names={"acme": "Acme SSO", "password": "Password"},
    sessions=RedisSessionStore(redis),
    transactions=RedisTransactionStore(redis),
    replay=RedisReplayStore(redis),
    csrf=RedisCsrfStore(redis),
    limiter=RedisRateLimiter(redis),
    trusted_origins=["https://app.example.com"],
    debug=DEBUG,
)

Mount the router and the middleware:

# myapp/main.py
from rn_forge.fastapi import FastApiApp, SessionMiddleware, auth_router
from rn_forge.fastapi.auth import sessions_for

from myapp.auth_config import config

app = FastApiApp(...)
app.add_middleware(SessionMiddleware, sessions=sessions_for(config))
app.include_router(auth_router(config))

sessions_for(config) builds the Sessions from the same stores and timeouts as the routes, so the middleware and the routes agree. SessionMiddleware resolves the session once per request and runs the CSRF check; a router mounted without it is unprotected, and current_principal raises RuntimeError for a session request. add_middleware wraps the application, so the middleware added last is outermost. Add SessionMiddleware before the middleware that should also decorate its responses (security headers, CORS), so a csrf-failed rejection, which the middleware answers itself, carries them.

When the router is mounted under a prefix other than /auth, tell the middleware the paths it has special rules for:

app.add_middleware(
    SessionMiddleware,
    sessions=sessions_for(config),
    untouched_paths=["/api/auth/session"],
    login_path="/api/auth/login/password",
    csrf_exempt_prefixes=["/api/auth/backchannel-logout/"],
)
app.include_router(auth_router(config, prefix="/api/auth"))

The session cookie is Secure, so serve development over localhost or HTTPS.

docs.title: Routes and responses
docs.text:
auth_router(config, prefix="/auth") serves these routes under the prefix. It is left out of the OpenAPI document. A 401 from any of them is a problem+json response with no WWW-Authenticate header.

Method Path Response GET providers 200, a list of {id, name, kind}. kind is oidc, oauth2, password or development; the development provider is listed only with debug=True GET login/{provider}?return_to= 302 to the identity provider, with the __Host-login-tx cookie. A return_to outside return_to_prefixes is replaced by default_return_to. An unknown provider is 404; login/password is 405 GET login/development?account= With debug=True only (otherwise 404): without account, an HTML list of the fixture accounts; with it, signs in and redirects to return_to GET callback/{provider} 302 to return_to, or to the error route; 429 when rate limited GET session 200 with the session body, or 401. Always sets the CSRF cookie POST logout 200 {"redirect": url or null}; 401 without a session POST logout/all 200 {"redirect": null}; 401 without a session POST backchannel-logout/{provider} 200; 400 for an invalid logout token; 404 for a provider with no handler POST login/password 200 with the session body, 401 for any failure, or 429

A callback error redirects to error_route (/auth/error) with ?error= set to one of access_denied, account_not_provisioned and login_failed. Details go to the log, never into the URL. A password login failure is one 401 whatever its cause, so the response does not reveal which accounts exist. The login body is JSON or form-encoded {username, password}.

The session body is camelCase: subject (the account ID), provider, roles, permissions, attributes, authTime, amr and expiresAt (the absolute timeout). Session responses carry Cache-Control: no-store.

The login transaction lives in its store for 10 minutes behind the __Host-login-tx cookie (HttpOnly, Secure, SameSite=Lax, Path=/, no Domain). A callback that carries more than one transaction cookie is rejected, and a transaction is consumed atomically, so a callback works once. The stores' synchronous calls and the Authlib providers run in the thread pool.

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
AuthRoutesConfig is a frozen dataclass. providers, accounts, contexts and account_state are required, and so is problem_type_base (a ValueError otherwise): it is the prefix of the type URI of the problem responses, which is what tells csrf-failed from forbidden.

Field Default URL prefix (auth_router(prefix=)) /auth return_to_prefixes / default_return_to ("/",) / / error_route /auth/error post_logout_redirect / idle_timeout / absolute_timeout 30 minutes / 12 hours trusted_origins / trusted_proxies none / none password_client_limit 30 per 5 minutes password_account_limit 10 per 5 minutes callback_client_limit 60 per 5 minutes sessions, transactions, replay, csrf, limiter in-memory stores, refused unless debug=True debug False Session cookie __Host-session, HttpOnly, Secure, SameSite=Lax, Path=/, no Domain Login transaction cookie __Host-login-tx, same flags, Max-Age=600 CSRF cookie / header XSRF-TOKEN (not HttpOnly, Secure, SameSite=Lax, Path=/) / X-XSRF-TOKEN Anonymous session lifetime 10 minutes

backchannel maps provider IDs to the back-channel logout handlers (rn_forge.auth.oidc.BackchannelLogout, which needs the oidc extra); provider_names maps IDs to display names; clock replaces the time source in tests.

trusted_proxies lists the peer addresses or CIDR networks, such as 10.0.0.0/8, whose X-Forwarded-Proto, X-Forwarded-Host and X-Forwarded-For headers are believed. From any other peer those headers are ignored, so a client cannot forge its own origin or address.

docs.title: Production storage
docs.text:
In-memory stores are held per process, so a second worker would not see a revocation, a transaction or a CSRF token. Outside debug, auth_router and Sessions refuse them with a RuntimeError naming the store: sessions, transactions, replay, CSRF and the rate limiter. Install the redis extra and use:

Store Class Login sessions rn_forge.auth.redis.RedisSessionStore Login transactions rn_forge.auth.redis.RedisTransactionStore Replayed token IDs and revoked sid values rn_forge.auth.redis.RedisReplayStore Authorization context versions rn_forge.auth.redis.RedisAuthorizationVersions CSRF tokens rn_forge.fastapi.auth.redis.RedisCsrfStore Rate limits rn_forge.fastapi.auth.redis.RedisRateLimiter

They take a redis.Redis client and need Redis 6.2 or later. The Redis modules of this package are not imported by rn_forge.fastapi, so a deployment without the extra can import the rest. RedisAuthorizationVersions goes to the AuthorizationContextCache, so that a change made in one process invalidates the cached context in every process; without it a change applies after the cache's ttl (60 seconds by default).

docs.title: Sessions and revocation
docs.text:
The login session is a rn-forge-auth SessionStore entry behind the __Host-session cookie. It holds the account ID, the account's session version at login, provider, issuer, external subject, auth_time, amr, session_ref and the ID token (only with rp_initiated_logout), and never permissions: those are computed on each request.

  • Timeouts. A 30-minute sliding idle timeout (idle_timeout) and a 12-hour absolute timeout (absolute_timeout). SessionMiddleware extends the idle expiry and refreshes the cookie on every request except GET /auth/session, so a client that polls the session does not keep it alive.
  • One read path. Sessions.read deletes the session, and the request is unauthenticated, when the absolute timeout has passed, the recorded session version differs from the account's, the account is inactive, or the session_ref is revoked. A cookie that names no valid session is cleared.
  • New IDs. Login replaces the session ID, and the CSRF token with it. Call await rotate_session(request) after a change to the account's privileges, so an ID seen before the change is useless afterwards; the middleware sets the new cookie.
  • Logout. /auth/logout ends the current session and starts a new anonymous one. /auth/logout/all and a back-channel logout that names only sub bump the account's session version through account_state, which ends every session of the account on its next request. A back-channel logout with a sid revokes that session only, until the absolute timeout. With rp_initiated_logout on the provider, /auth/logout returns the identity provider's end-session URL.
  • Disabling. contexts.set_active(account_id, False) (or any change that makes the account inactive) ends the account's sessions at their next request.

active_session(request) returns the ActiveSession (the SessionInfo and the account's current authorization context) the middleware resolved, or None.

docs.title: CSRF
docs.text:
Unsafe methods on session-authenticated routes are protected by a synchronizer token, which SessionMiddleware checks for the /auth routes and for the application's own routes alike. The token is random and kept in the CsrfStore under the session ID; the readable XSRF-TOKEN cookie hands it to the browser, and the request repeats it in X-XSRF-TOKEN, which are Angular's defaults. The comparison is constant-time.

  • GET /auth/session always sets the cookie, including when it answers 401. With no session it starts an anonymous session, a 10-minute entry behind __Host-session that holds only a token, so POST /auth/login/password is protected before sign-in.
  • Login replaces the session ID and the token; logout starts a new anonymous session with a new token; rotate_session carries the token to the new ID.
  • Checked: an unsafe request that carries the __Host-session cookie, whether it names a live session, an anonymous one or nothing known, and a request to the password login path (login_path), which a browser can reach with no cookie.
  • Exempt: GET, HEAD, OPTIONS and TRACE; a request with a Bearer Authorization header; the paths under csrf_exempt_prefixes (back-channel logout, which carries a signed token); and a request with no session cookie to an application route, which has no session to ride. A Basic header is not exempt: browsers replay cached Basic credentials on their own.
  • Origin. The Origin header (the Referer over HTTPS when there is no Origin) must be the request's own origin or one of trusted_origins, and Sec-Fetch-Site: cross-site is rejected even from a trusted origin. The request's own scheme and host come from X-Forwarded-Proto and X-Forwarded-Host only when the peer is in trusted_proxies.
  • A rejection is the 403 csrf-failed problem; its reason is logged, never sent.

docs.title: Authentication
docs.text:
current_principal(bearer=None) returns a dependency that yields a Principal from the login session (mechanism="session", the account's roles and permissions from its authorization context, and the session's auth_time and amr), or from a bearer token when bearer is given.

bearer_auth verifies an externally issued token, then resolves its (issuer, subject) through AccountResolver.lookup. It never provisions: a token with no linked account, or whose account is inactive, is 401. The principal's subject is the account ID, its roles, tenant and attributes come from the authorization context, and its permissions are the account's, limited to what the token's scopes allow through scope_map:

from rn_forge.auth.oidc import OidcAuthenticator
from rn_forge.fastapi.auth import bearer_auth, current_principal

from myapp.auth_config import config, contexts

bearer = bearer_auth(
    authenticator=OidcAuthenticator.from_issuer(
        "https://login.example.com/tenant/v2.0", audience="api://orders"
    ),
    accounts=config.accounts,
    contexts=contexts,
    scope_map={"orders:read": frozenset({"orders.list", "orders.read"})},
)
caller = current_principal(bearer=bearer)

Build the authenticator once at startup: it holds the JWKS cache.

One credential per request. A request with an Authorization header is authenticated by bearer alone: an invalid token is 401 even with a valid session cookie, and without bearer the header makes the request unauthenticated. Any other request is authenticated by the session. An unauthenticated request is 401 with the Bearer challenge when bearer is given, and without a challenge otherwise, and the failure reason goes to the log callback, never the response.

basic_auth(authenticator=...) is the RFC 7617 twin for an authenticator you supply and does not link accounts. It is for local development and simple internal deployments only.

docs.title: Authorization
docs.text:
requires(caller, Requirement(...)) authenticates, then enforces the requirement with rn_forge.auth.ScopeAuthorizer (or the authorizer you pass). Insufficient access is a 403 with no challenge. requires_permission(caller, permission_key, action) enforces the key that rn_forge.auth.requirement_for builds from the base key and an explicit action, list, retrieve or partial_update for example; action_map overrides the default action-to-verb map:

from fastapi import APIRouter, Depends
from rn_forge.auth import Principal, Requirement
from rn_forge.fastapi.auth import requires, requires_permission

router = APIRouter()


@router.get("/orders")
async def list_orders(
    principal: Principal = Depends(requires_permission(caller, "orders", "list")),
): ...


@router.post("/reports")
async def run_report(
    principal: Principal = Depends(
        requires(caller, Requirement(all_scopes=frozenset({"reports:run"})))
    ),
): ...

PolicyGuard(policy, hides_existence=False) applies a ResourcePolicy. guard.scope(principal, action, query) narrows a query of any type, such as a SQLAlchemy select, so rows, counts and pages cover only permitted rows; guard.check(principal, action, obj) returns the object or raises 403, or 404 when hides_existence is true:

from rn_forge.fastapi.auth import PolicyGuard
from sqlalchemy import select

guard = PolicyGuard(OrderPolicy(), hides_existence=True)


@router.get("/orders/{order_id}")
async def get_order(
    order_id: int,
    principal: Principal = Depends(caller),
    session: Session = Depends(db_session),
):
    order = session.scalar(
        guard.scope(principal, "retrieve", select(Order).where(Order.id == order_id))
    )
    if order is None:
        raise LookupError("Not found")
    return guard.check(principal, "retrieve", order)

docs.title: Rate limits and audit events
docs.text:
POST /auth/login/password and GET /auth/callback/{provider} are rate limited with a fixed-window counter in limiter. The client is the connection's peer, or the nearest address in X-Forwarded-For that is not a trusted proxy when the peer is in trusted_proxies. Password login is limited per client and per submitted username (hashed in the key); callbacks per client only, because no account is known before the response is verified. Each limit is a RateLimit(limit, window), or None for none. A limited request is the 429 too-many-requests problem with Retry-After. Windows are aligned to the clock, so a client can use a limit twice around a window boundary.

Security-relevant events are INFO records on the rn_forge.audit.auth channel, in the form audit event=<name> key='value' ...:

Event Emitted when login.success A login starts a session login.failure A login fails (provider, code, reason) logout, logout.all, logout.backchannel A session or sessions end account.provisioned A provisioning resolver creates an account account.rejected The resolver refuses an identity account.disabled An inactive account logs in authorization.denied requires, requires_permission or PolicyGuard denies a request rate_limited A request is answered 429

Events carry account IDs, provider IDs, codes and short reasons, and never a token, code, assertion, password, session ID or email address.

docs.title: What the application implements
docs.text:
The binding takes these rn_forge.auth protocols; every method is synchronous and runs in the thread pool.

  • AccountResolver. resolve(identity) links, provisions or rejects an external identity at login and returns the account ID, raising AccountRejected to refuse it; lookup(issuer, subject) is the read-only form bearer_auth uses. A resolver that creates accounts records account.provisioned once the account is committed:

    ```python from rn_forge.auth import audit

    audit("account.provisioned", account_id=account.id, provider=identity.provider) ```

  • AuthorizationContextProvider. resolve(account_id) returns the AuthorizationContext: active, session_version, permissions, roles and attributes. Wrap it in an AuthorizationContextCache and call contexts.invalidate(account_id) when a role or permission changes.

  • AccountStateWriter. set_active(account_id, active) and bump_session_version(account_id) persist the state the context carries. /auth/logout/all and a back-channel logout call them; the cache above writes through to it.
  • ResourcePolicy. allows(principal, action, resource) and scope(principal, action, query), for PolicyGuard.
  • PasswordVerifier. For PasswordIdentityProvider: a callable (username, password) -> subject | None. Hash comparison and the user lookup are yours.

docs.title: Soft delete
docs.text:
rn_forge.fastapi serves AIP-164 soft delete: DELETE {collection}/{id} soft-deletes and answers 200 with the resource, POST {collection}/{id}:undelete restores it, and showDeleted brings deleted resources back into a list. The wire contract is §21 of rn-forge-web's API conventions. Persistence is the application's: soft_delete_router takes a store, a dependency that returns an object with these methods:

Store method Contract find(id) A SoftDeleteState of row, version (None when unversioned) and delete_time, or None when the resource does not exist. Deleted rows are found. soft_delete(id) Soft-deletes the row and returns it. undelete(id) Restores the row and returns it.

The store owns the transaction and the clock. The router checks the resource's state first (404 or 409), then If-Match on a versioned row (428, 400 or 412), and only then calls the store to write. It answers with response_model dumped by alias, and the new ETag read back through find.

docs.title: Over SQLAlchemy
docs.text:
The code below is application code. It joins rn-forge-fastapi and rn-forge-sqlalchemy, which do not import each other.

from datetime import datetime

from fastapi import Depends
from sqlalchemy import select
from sqlalchemy.ext.asyncio import async_sessionmaker
from sqlalchemy.orm import Mapped, mapped_column

from rn_forge.fastapi import (
    SoftDeleteState,
    show_deleted_param,
    soft_delete_router,
)
from rn_forge.sqlalchemy import (
    AuditMixin,
    Base,
    SoftDeleteMixin,
    VersionMixin,
    live,
    soft_delete,
    undelete,
)
from rn_forge.web import Page, WireModel, require_live


class Note(SoftDeleteMixin, VersionMixin, AuditMixin, Base):
    __tablename__ = "note"

    id: Mapped[str] = mapped_column(primary_key=True)
    text: Mapped[str]


class NoteOut(WireModel):
    id: str
    text: str
    delete_time: datetime | None = None


class NoteStore:
    def __init__(self, sessions: async_sessionmaker, actor: str) -> None:
        self.sessions, self.actor = sessions, actor

    async def find(self, id: str) -> SoftDeleteState | None:
        async with self.sessions() as session:
            note = await session.get(Note, id)
        return None if note is None else SoftDeleteState(note, note.version, note.delete_time)

    async def soft_delete(self, id: str) -> Note:
        return await self._write(id, soft_delete)

    async def undelete(self, id: str) -> Note:
        return await self._write(id, undelete)

    async def _write(self, id, change) -> Note:
        async with self.sessions() as session:
            note = await session.get(Note, id)
            change(note, actor=self.actor)
            await session.commit()
            return note


app.include_router(
    soft_delete_router(
        "/notes",
        response_model=NoteOut,
        resource_label="Note",
        store=get_note_store,  # a dependency returning a NoteStore
        require_if_match=True,
    )
)


@app.get("/notes", response_model=Page[NoteOut])
async def list_notes(show_deleted: bool = Depends(show_deleted_param())): ...

The list route reads showDeleted with show_deleted_param() and passes it to live(select(Note), Note, show_deleted=show_deleted). The application's own PUT and PATCH routes call require_live(note.delete_time, label="Note", id=id) before anything else that can fail. batch_delete_router needs no change: its store's find returns only live ids and its delete_many soft-deletes them, so a deleted id is a 404 for the whole batch.

docs.title: Tabular export, import and batch operations
docs.text:
rn_forge.fastapi.transfer serves spreadsheet download and upload, an import template, and batch get, create, update and delete. It needs the transfer extra (rn-forge-data, which brings tablib and openpyxl, and python-multipart) and is not imported by rn_forge.fastapi. The wire contract is §17 of rn-forge-web's API conventions. Persistence is the application's: each route factory takes a store, a dependency that returns an object with the methods the factory calls.

Factory Route Store Store methods import_router POST {collection}:import ImportStore import_rows(rows, *, validate_only) import_template_router GET {collection}:importTemplate TemplateSource rows() batch_create_router POST {collection}:batchCreate BatchCreateStore create_many(items) batch_delete_router POST {collection}:batchDelete BatchDeleteStore find(ids), delete_many(ids) batch_get_router GET {collection}:batchGet BatchGetStore get_many(ids) batch_update_router POST {collection}:batchUpdate BatchUpdateStore current(ids), update_many(items)

The stores are structural protocols, so a store never imports them. A factory validates the request, applies the row cap (max_rows) and calls the store only with data that passed. The store makes the writes. Because the store is obtained through Depends, it can take a database session, the principal or filter parameters the ordinary FastAPI way. Every factory also takes dependencies= for route-level dependencies such as authorization.

docs.title: A complete resource
docs.text:
The code below is application code, not part of rn-forge. It joins rn-forge-fastapi and rn-forge-sqlalchemy, which do not import each other: the application's store calls upsert and keyset, and rn-forge-fastapi calls the store. It serves /orders with a paged list, CSV and xlsx export, import, import template, batch create and batch delete.

The model and the three wire models. OrderImport's aliases are the spreadsheet headers, and it also serves as the export and template model, so a downloaded file can be uploaded again.

from collections.abc import Sequence

from fastapi import Depends, FastAPI
from pydantic import ConfigDict, Field
from sqlalchemy import delete, select
from sqlalchemy.ext.asyncio import AsyncSession, async_sessionmaker, create_async_engine
from sqlalchemy.orm import Mapped, mapped_column

from rn_forge.fastapi import order_by_param, page_params, register_problem_handlers
from rn_forge.fastapi.transfer import (
    batch_create_router,
    batch_delete_router,
    import_router,
    import_template_router,
    tabular_format,
    tabular_export,
)
from rn_forge.sqlalchemy import AuditMixin, Base, keyset, next_page_token, upsert
from rn_forge.web import ItemsDenied, Page, WireModel
from rn_forge.web.transfer import ImportCounts


class Order(AuditMixin, Base):
    __tablename__ = "orders"

    id: Mapped[int] = mapped_column(primary_key=True)
    order_no: Mapped[str] = mapped_column(unique=True)
    name: Mapped[str]
    quantity: Mapped[int]


class OrderImport(WireModel):  # columns: the spreadsheet's headers
    model_config = ConfigDict(populate_by_name=True)

    order_no: str = Field(alias="Order No", serialization_alias="Order No")
    name: str = Field(alias="Name", serialization_alias="Name")
    quantity: int = Field(alias="Quantity", serialization_alias="Quantity")


class OrderCreate(WireModel):  # one item of :batchCreate
    order_no: str
    name: str
    quantity: int = 0


class OrderOut(WireModel):  # one created or listed order
    order_no: str
    name: str
    quantity: int

The store. It opens its own session for each operation, so each operation is one transaction that it commits or discards itself.

SORT_ATTRS = {"orderNo": "order_no", "name": "name"}


class OrderStore:
    """Implements ImportStore, TemplateSource, BatchCreateStore and BatchDeleteStore."""

    def __init__(self, sessions: async_sessionmaker[AsyncSession], actor: str) -> None:
        self.sessions = sessions
        self.actor = actor

    async def import_rows(
        self, rows: Sequence[OrderImport], *, validate_only: bool
    ) -> ImportCounts:
        async with self.sessions() as session:
            counts = await upsert(
                session,
                Order,
                [row.model_dump(by_alias=False) for row in rows],
                key=["order_no"],
                fields=["name", "quantity"],
                actor=self.actor,
            )
            if validate_only:
                await session.rollback()
            else:
                await session.commit()
        return ImportCounts(counts.created, counts.updated, counts.skipped)

    async def rows(self) -> Sequence[Order]:
        async with self.sessions() as session:
            return (await session.scalars(select(Order).order_by(Order.id))).all()

    async def create_many(self, items: Sequence[OrderCreate]) -> Sequence[Order]:
        denied = {
            str(i): ["You may not create this order."]
            for i, item in enumerate(items)
            if item.name.startswith("internal-")
        }
        if denied:
            raise ItemsDenied(denied, root="requests")
        created = [Order(**item.model_dump(by_alias=False), created_by=self.actor) for item in items]
        async with self.sessions() as session:
            session.add_all(created)
            await session.commit()
        return created

    async def find(self, ids: Sequence[str]) -> list[str]:
        async with self.sessions() as session:
            stmt = select(Order.order_no).where(Order.order_no.in_(ids))
            return list(await session.scalars(stmt))

    async def delete_many(self, ids: Sequence[str]) -> None:
        async with self.sessions() as session:
            await session.execute(delete(Order).where(Order.order_no.in_(ids)))
            await session.commit()

    async def page(self, size, cursor, terms) -> Page[OrderOut]:
        stmt = keyset(
            select(Order),
            columns={"orderNo": Order.order_no, "name": Order.name},
            terms=terms,
            cursor=cursor,
            id_column=Order.id,
        )
        async with self.sessions() as session:
            found = (await session.scalars(stmt.limit(size + 1))).all()
        window = found[:size]
        token = None
        if len(found) > size:
            last = window[-1]
            values = [getattr(last, SORT_ATTRS[t.field]) for t in terms]
            token = next_page_token(values, last.id, terms)
        return Page[OrderOut](
            items=[OrderOut.model_validate(o, from_attributes=True) for o in window],
            next_page_token=token,
        )

The wiring.

def build_app() -> FastAPI:
    engine = create_async_engine("sqlite+aiosqlite://")
    sessions = async_sessionmaker(engine, expire_on_commit=False)

    def order_store() -> OrderStore:
        return OrderStore(sessions, actor="alice")

    app = FastAPI()
    register_problem_handlers(app)
    app.include_router(import_router("/orders", model=OrderImport, store=order_store, max_rows=5000))
    app.include_router(import_template_router("/orders", model=OrderImport, source=order_store, max_rows=5000))
    app.include_router(batch_create_router("/orders", model=OrderCreate, response_model=OrderOut, resource_name="orders", store=order_store, max_rows=100))
    app.include_router(batch_delete_router("/orders", resource_label="Order", store=order_store, max_rows=100))

    @app.get("/orders")
    async def list_orders(
        fmt=Depends(tabular_format(("csv", "xlsx"))),
        params=Depends(page_params(cap=100, default=50)),
        terms=Depends(order_by_param(allowed=["orderNo", "name"])),
        store: OrderStore = Depends(order_store),
    ):
        if fmt is not None:
            return await tabular_export(await store.rows(), OrderImport, fmt, f"orders.{fmt.extension}", max_rows=5000, instance="/orders")
        return await store.page(*params, terms)

    return app

docs.title: All or nothing, and validateOnly
docs.text:
Each store method does all its writes in one session and commits once, at the end:

  • import_rows runs upsert, which never commits. A real import then commits. validateOnly rolls back instead, so the report shows the true created, updated and skipped counts and nothing is persisted. Any exception leaves the async with block before the commit, which discards the session's work.
  • create_many checks every item for permission before it adds any, and raises ItemsDenied if one is refused: a 403 whose errors[].pointer is /requests/<i>. A database error before the commit discards the batch the same way.
  • delete_many is one DELETE and one commit. The factory has already called find and answered a 404 for the first id that does not exist.

The factories do not open transactions, since they do not know the persistence layer. A store that shares a request-scoped session instead must roll that session back itself when it fails or when validate_only is set.

A row that fails a check only the store can make, such as a foreign-key lookup, is reported by raising RowsInvalid(errors) (from rn_forge.web, built from rn_forge.web.transfer.RowError) from import_rows. It renders the same 422 as a cell that failed validation, pointing at /rows/<row>/<column>.

docs.title: Batch get and update
docs.text:
batch_get_router reads a repeated ids query parameter. The store's get_many(ids) returns the rows that exist within the caller's scope, keyed by id as a string. batch_update_router takes {"requests": [{"id", "patch", "ifMatch"}]}: the store's current(ids) returns each existing row as an object with row and version (None when the resource is unversioned), the factory merges each patch into the row dumped through model by alias and validates the result as model, and update_many(items) receives (id, model instance) pairs only after every check has passed. It writes them in one transaction, bumps each version and returns the updated rows in the order given.

app.include_router(batch_get_router("/orders", response_model=OrderOut, resource_name="orders", resource_label="Order", store=order_store, max_rows=100))
app.include_router(batch_update_router("/orders", model=OrderDocument, response_model=OrderOut, resource_name="orders", resource_label="Order", store=order_store, max_rows=100, require_if_match=True))

update_many raises ItemsDenied(errors, root="requests") before writing to refuse an item. codec= changes the validator format of ifMatch, which defaults to VersionETagCodec.

docs.title: What the factories answer
docs.text:
Request Response :import succeeds 200 {created, updated, skipped, validateOnly} :import has no file part 422, errors[].pointer /file, This field is required. :import has an unsupported or unreadable file 422 at /file with the shared detail :import has a failed cell 422, errors[].pointer /rows/<row>/<column>; the store is not called :import or a batch is over max_rows 422, The import exceeds the limit of N rows. or The batch exceeds the limit of N rows., no errors member a batch request has no requests or ids member 422 at /requests or /ids, This field is required. the member is an empty list or not a list 422 at the member, A non-empty list is required. :batchCreate item fails validation 422, every failed field at /requests/<i>/<field>; the store is not called :batchCreate raises ItemsDenied 403, errors[].pointer /requests/<i> :batchCreate succeeds 200 {"<resource_name>": [...]} of response_model dumped by alias :batchGet has no non-empty ids, or more than max_rows 400, A non-empty ids parameter is required. or The batch exceeds the limit of N rows. :batchGet or :batchUpdate names an unknown id 404, {resource_label} {id} not found :batchGet succeeds 200 {"<resource_name>": [...]} in request order, duplicates repeated :batchUpdate item is malformed or repeats an id 422, every failing item at /requests/<i>/id, /patch or /ifMatch; the store is not called :batchUpdate precondition fails 428, 400 or 412, errors[].pointer /requests/<i>/ifMatch :batchUpdate merged document is invalid 422, every failed field at /requests/<i>/patch/<field>; the store is not asked to write :batchUpdate raises ItemsDenied 403, errors[].pointer /requests/<i> :batchUpdate succeeds 200 {"<resource_name>": [...]} of response_model dumped by alias, in request order :batchDelete names an unknown id 404, {resource_label} {id} not found :batchDelete succeeds 204

These need register_problem_handlers(app), which renders RowsInvalid, ItemsDenied and the request validation errors as application/problem+json.

docs.title: Export
docs.text:
tabular_format() is a dependency that negotiates Accept or ?format=. A None result means the client wants the JSON list. tabular_export answers a tabular request from a list route: the file, or a 422 when there are more rows than max_rows.

The export model is a pydantic model. Its serialization_aliases are the column headers, and a computed_field is a column, which covers foreign-key traversal, full names and enum display names. Rows are validated with from_attributes=True, so ORM objects work directly. CSV is streamed; xlsx is written with rn_forge.data.write_xlsx. tabular_response is the same without the cap, for a route that applies its own.

docs.title: Reading a file yourself
docs.text: read_rows loads an UploadFile (csv, tsv or xlsx) and validates each row against a pydantic model whose aliases are the external headers. A bad cell is never raised: RowsResult.errors holds a RowError for each, valid holds the rows that passed and total counts the data rows. An unsupported or unreadable file raises ValueError with the shared detail. The tablib work and per-row validation run in a worker thread. A route that needs more than import_router offers can call it and answer with problem_response(row_errors_problem(...)).

docs.title: Paging a SQLAlchemy list
docs.text: order_by_param and page_params parse the request, rn-forge-sqlalchemy's keyset applies them to a Select, and next_page_token writes the next token. The page method of the store above does this: it fetches size + 1 rows to learn whether another page exists. keyset takes the sort column and the unique id column, so the order is stable when the sort column repeats.

docs.title: Conformance
docs.text: tests/test_conformance.py serves /conformance/orders* and /conformance/capped* through these factories over one in-memory store, and passes every transfer.* case in the shared table. The rn-forge-sqlalchemy test suite serves an application over SQLite and passes the pagination and import cases.

docs.title: Wiring an application
docs.text: Promoted from rn-forge-web's interim FastAPI wiring guide, which was written to become this package. What was a page of copy-paste handler, dependency and router code there is a handful of calls here; what is left is the wiring an application genuinely owns.

docs.title: The wiring module
docs.text:
from fastapi import APIRouter, FastAPI

from rn_forge.fastapi import (
    AppConfig,
    FastApiApp,
)
from rn_forge.web import ProblemType, default_registry

from myapp.errors import OrderLocked
from myapp.settings import Settings


def build_app(*, settings: Settings, checks) -> FastAPI:
    registry = default_registry(type_base=settings.problem_type_base)
    registry.register(OrderLocked, ProblemType("order-locked", 409, "Order Locked"))

    return FastApiApp(
        AppConfig(
            registry=registry,
            checks=checks,
            required_checks=("db",),
            realm="orders",
            log=settings.log,
        ),
        routers=(orders.router,),
        title="Orders",
    )

FastApiApp installs the common adapters only. The application's composition root constructs Settings, checks, routers and infrastructure explicitly, so tests can pass fakes and the factory never reads the environment or starts a resource.

docs.title: The rules the wiring depends on
docs.text:
1. Register domain exceptions on the registry before creating AppConfig. Handlers are registered per exception type, because Starlette re-raises anything handled by an Exception handler. A row added later still renders correctly, but as a logged, re-raised server error.
  2. Pass that registry to AppConfig. Its statuses are the problem responses the schema declares on every operation.
  3. Tracing. FastApiApp instruments itself with FastAPIInstrumentor.instrument_app by default (AppConfig.tracing), after the kit's own middleware, so the instrumentation wraps the whole stack regardless of add order. It also sets a TraceResponsePropagator as the global response propagator, but only when nothing else has — an application that configures its own response propagator first is left alone. FastApiApp turns off FastAPI's native tracing unless the application passes telemetry=, so AppConfig.tracing alone decides whether server spans are recorded. Configure a TracerProvider and exporter in the application, or run under opentelemetry-instrument; FastApiApp never does either.
  4. Derive every model from rn_forge.web.WireModel. camelCase on the wire is enforced by the base class, including in a hand-built JSONResponse(model.model_dump(mode="json")).
  5. Spell a non-CRUD route as a custom method. POST /orders/{order_id}:cancel is named ordersCancel automatically, on both stacks. The same action as a plain path segment (/orders/{order_id}/cancel) is indistinguishable from a sub-collection and needs an explicit operation_id=.

docs.title: Routes
docs.text:
from typing import Annotated

from fastapi import APIRouter, Depends

from rn_forge.fastapi import bearer_auth, page_params, require_if_match, requires
from rn_forge.auth import Principal, Requirement
from rn_forge.web import Cursor, Page, check_precondition

router = APIRouter()
caller = bearer_auth(authenticator=jwt_authenticator, log=log)
reader = requires(caller, Requirement(all_scopes=frozenset({"orders:read"})))


@router.get("/orders")
async def orders_list(
    page: Annotated[tuple[int, Cursor | None], Depends(page_params(cap=100, default=20))],
    principal: Annotated[Principal, Depends(reader)],
) -> Page[OrderOut]:
    size, cursor = page                    # size already clamped; cursor already decoded
    ...


@router.patch("/orders/{order_id}")
async def orders_update(order_id: str, if_match: Annotated[str, Depends(require_if_match())]):
    order = await repo.get(order_id)
    check_precondition(if_match, current_version=order.version, entity_id=order_id, required=True)
    ...

Page[OrderOut] reaches the schema as pydantic's own name, Page_OrderOut_ — document text is not held identical across stacks (only wire behaviour and operationId are; see api-conventions.md §9). The DRF binding names its own paginated component its own way too, PaginatedOrderOutList.

pageSize above the cap is clamped, never rejected — do not add a Query(le=...) alongside page_params; that is a 422 and a specification violation.

docs.title: Merge patch
docs.text:
merge_patch_body() checks the media type and returns the raw body; merge_into parses it, merges it into the current resource and validates the result against the model. merge_patch_openapi() declares the request body. Declare merge_patch_body() before the If-Match dependency, so the media type answers first (415), and call check_precondition before merge_into, so a stale request is 412 whatever the body says.

from fastapi import Depends, Header

from rn_forge.fastapi import merge_into, merge_patch_body, merge_patch_openapi
from rn_forge.web import check_precondition


@router.patch("/documents/{doc_id}", openapi_extra=merge_patch_openapi())
async def documents_update(
    doc_id: str,
    body: bytes = Depends(merge_patch_body()),
    if_match: str | None = Header(default=None),
) -> DocumentOut:
    document = await repo.get(doc_id)
    check_precondition(if_match, current_version=document.version, entity_id=doc_id)
    return merge_into(DocumentOut, document, body)

Use require_if_match() in place of the optional header to make it required (428). A null on a non-nullable field is a 422 that reads This field may not be null.

docs.title: Partial responses
docs.text:
read_mask_param(Model) is a dependency yielding the parsed readMask, or None for the whole resource. It reads the model's aliases, so a nested model, Model | None or list[Model] field can be reached with a dotted path and anything else is a leaf. A path that names nothing is a 400 problem before the route runs. Apply the mask to the dumped body with mask.apply(...), or to a page with masked(page, mask). Return a JSONResponse and declare response_model for the documentation, because the pruned body no longer validates as the full model.

from fastapi import Depends
from fastapi.responses import JSONResponse

from rn_forge.fastapi import masked, read_mask_param
from rn_forge.web import Page, ReadMask


@router.get("/profiles/{profile_id}", response_model=ProfileOut)
async def profiles_get(
    profile_id: str, mask: ReadMask | None = Depends(read_mask_param(ProfileOut))
) -> JSONResponse:
    body = ProfileOut.model_validate(await repo.get(profile_id)).model_dump(by_alias=True)
    return JSONResponse(body if mask is None else mask.apply(body))


@router.get("/profiles", response_model=Page[ProfileOut])
async def profiles_list(
    mask: ReadMask | None = Depends(read_mask_param(ProfileOut)),
) -> JSONResponse:
    page = Page[ProfileOut](items=await repo.list(), next_page_token=None)
    return JSONResponse(masked(page, mask))

batch_get_router accepts readMask unless it is built with read_mask=False.

docs.title: Security headers
docs.text: FastApiApp installs the OWASP REST Security Cheat Sheet response headers by default (AppConfig.security_headers). Strict-Transport-Security is excluded from the default preset and is opt-in — AppConfig(hsts=True) — for a deployment that terminates TLS itself rather than behind a front end that already sets it.

docs.title: Service discovery
docs.text: FastApiApp serves RFC 9727's /.well-known/api-catalog by default (AppConfig.api_catalog), pointing at the OpenAPI document (openapi_url) and docs UI (docs_url) it already serves, plus readiness. Set AppConfig(api_catalog=False) to turn it off.

docs.title: CORS
docs.text:
Opt-in, and the application owns the policy:

from rn_forge.fastapi import AppConfig, CorsPolicy

config = AppConfig(cors=CorsPolicy(allow_origins=("https://app.example.com",)))

CorsPolicy.expose_headers defaults to rn_forge.web.EXPOSED_HEADERS — the response headers this kit emits that a browser cannot read unless a CORS policy names them (ETag, Link, Content-Disposition, and so on). traceresponse needs no entry here — the OpenTelemetry response propagator exposes it itself. allow_origins has no default; naming them is the application's decision. CorsPolicy(allow_credentials=True, allow_origins=("*",)) raises — browsers reject that combination.

from datetime import UTC, datetime

from rn_forge.fastapi import deprecated

SUNSET_ANNOUNCED = datetime(2026, 1, 1, tzinfo=UTC)
SUNSET_DATE = datetime(2026, 7, 1, tzinfo=UTC)


@router.get(
    "/orders/legacy-summary",
    deprecated=True,  # marks the OpenAPI operation
    dependencies=[
        Depends(deprecated(deprecated_at=SUNSET_ANNOUNCED, sunset=SUNSET_DATE))
    ],
)
async def orders_legacy_summary(): ...

deprecated=True and the deprecated(...) dependency are both needed: one marks the document, the other stamps the Deprecation/Sunset/Link headers on the wire (RFC 9745, RFC 8594).

docs.title: Publishing a model no route references
docs.text:
A generated client sometimes needs a shape that never appears as a request or response body — a webhook payload, an event published to a queue. Override openapi() on a FastApiApp subclass and call super().openapi() first, the same composition FastApiApp itself uses to repair the document:

from pydantic.json_schema import models_json_schema


class MyApp(FastApiApp):
    def openapi(self):
        schema = super().openapi()
        _, definitions = models_json_schema(
            [(OrderShippedEvent, "serialization")],
            ref_template="#/components/schemas/{model}",
        )
        schema["components"]["schemas"].update(definitions.get("$defs", {}))
        return schema

docs.title: What an application still writes
docs.text:
• The authenticator — unless it is OIDC. For bearer tokens from an identity provider, install rn-forge-fastapi[oidc] and use the shared implementation rather than writing one:

    ```python from rn_forge.auth.oidc import OidcAuthenticator

    authenticator = OidcAuthenticator.from_issuer( "https://idp.example.com/tenant", audience="api://orders" ) caller = bearer_auth(authenticator=authenticator, log=log) ```

    Pass caller to requires(caller, Requirement(all_scopes=...)), then use the returned dependency on protected routes. FastApiApp registers the problem handlers that render authentication failures as 401 with a challenge and authorization failures as 403 without one.

    Build it once at startup — it holds the JWKS cache. It is the same authenticator rn-forge-django uses, so both stacks accept the same tokens. For any other scheme, bearer_auth takes any rn_forge.auth.Authenticator or AsyncAuthenticator: verify the token, map claims to a Principal, and raise AuthenticationFailed with the reason — the reason reaches log, never the body. A sync Authenticator runs in the threadpool, so a blocking JWKS fetch does not stall the event loop. basic_auth is for local development and simple internal deployments only.

  • The idempotency store. Implement rn_forge.web.AsyncIdempotencyStore over the application's database. Race safety comes from a UNIQUE (scope, key) constraint with INSERT … ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING and a read-back, never a check-then-insert. Decorate the route with idempotent(store, scope=...) (rn_forge.fastapi.idempotent), which wraps rn_forge.web.run_idempotent_async: the decorated route takes request: Request and returns a Response.

    ```python from fastapi import Request from fastapi.responses import JSONResponse from rn_forge.fastapi import idempotent

    @router.post("/charges", status_code=201) @idempotent(store, scope="charges") async def create_charge(request: Request, body: ChargeIn) -> JSONResponse: ... ```

  • The checks. Zero-argument callables, sync or async, returning a bool or a rn_forge.web.CheckResult. Pass health_router(timeout=...) so a hung dependency is reported as fail rather than hanging /readyz; the default, None, waits indefinitely.

docs.title: rn_forge.fastapi.auth.csrf
docs.text:
Synchronizer-token CSRF protection for the session-authenticated routes.

The token is a random value kept server-side under the session ID, and handed to the browser in the readable XSRF-TOKEN cookie. :class:CsrfProtection compares it in constant time with the X-XSRF-TOKEN header on an unsafe request, which are the names Angular's HttpClient uses. Before sign-in the record is keyed by an anonymous ID behind the __Host-session cookie, so the login request is protected too. SessionMiddleware decides which requests are checked: those that carry the session cookie, and the password-login path.

The request's Origin (Referer over HTTPS when there is no Origin) must be its own origin or one of trusted_origins, and Sec-Fetch-Site: cross-site is rejected. The request's own scheme and host come from X-Forwarded-Proto and X-Forwarded-Host only when the peer is one of trusted_proxies. A request with a Bearer Authorization header skips the check.

docs.text:
The login session, kept in an rn-forge-auth :class:~rn_forge.auth.SessionStore.

The session ID travels in the __Host-session cookie. Every store call is synchronous; :class:Sessions methods are blocking and async code runs them in the thread pool. :class:SessionMiddleware resolves the session once per request and keeps its cookie current.

GET requests to the paths in untouched_paths read the session without extending it; every other request moves the idle expiry forward.

The middleware also runs the :class:~rn_forge.fastapi.auth.csrf.CsrfProtection check on an unsafe request that carries the session cookie, or that goes to the password-login path, so the application's own session-authenticated routes are protected as well as the /auth routes. A request with no session cookie reaches the application unchecked.

An unsafe request is then checked with sessions.csrf when it carries the session cookie, whether it names a live session, a live anonymous session or nothing known, or when its path is login_path, which a browser can reach with no cookie. A failure is answered with the 403 csrf-failed problem. A request to a path under csrf_exempt_prefixes is not checked.

docs.title: rotate_session(request) async
docs.text:
Give the request's session a new ID and keep its content.

Call it after a change of the account's privileges, so a session ID that was seen before the change is useless afterwards. The middleware sets the new cookie on the response. A request with no session is left alone.

Raises:

Type Description RuntimeError

:class:SessionMiddleware is not installed.
